P01.passage: Last spring, the council of one river town replaced the property tax that paid for trash pickup with a monthly fee charged to each household. Bills explained the charge line by line, larger, costlier homes paid more than small ones, and the fee just covered the cost of hauling. But the first bill, mailed in June, also charged every household for pickups going back to January, months before the council had voted. Several council members objected that the fee, as written, was ______.
P01.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P02.passage: In 1724 two rival port cities signed an agreement on the use of each other's harbors. It was signed at a feast after a procession of both councils, and its clauses repeated pledges of friendship while setting no fees, rules, or penalties; at that moment each city was seizing the other's ships, and harbor traffic went on exactly as before. Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.
P02.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P03.passage: Early in the last century, a one-room press in a river town printed poetry in editions of a few hundred copies. It opened in 1919, when the local poets had only begun experimenting, and its editor returned every manuscript with pages of notes urging plainer speech and local subjects; the poets, who met in a cafe across the river, rewrote their poems along those lines, and a city firm published their books to quick success. One historian of the town's literary life argues that the press ______ the plain-spoken regional poetry that flourished there in the 1920s.
P03.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P04.passage: In 1983 a small company released the operating system that would run its office computers for the next decade. It was built as one tightly interlocked program that crashed whenever a single part failed, and it was the most advanced system of its day; but the company kept its code secret and sued any rival that copied even a few of its commands. Engineers who studied the system years later described it, above all, as ______.
P04.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P05.passage: In 1931 a touring company staged a new version of a little-known seventeenth-century tragedy about a queen torn between duty and love. The company kept every scene in the order the author wrote it and performed each with grave sincerity, but it added a long prologue and two new scenes of its own, so the evening ran nearly an hour past the running time the text alone required. One reviewer who knew the original text well wrote that the production had ______ the play.
P05.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P06.passage: In 1838 a provincial assembly passed a law governing disputes between landowners and the tenant farmers who rented their fields. It ordered every pending eviction case suspended for ten years without a hearing, so tenants and landowners simply waited; when the decade ended, the same quarrels returned to the village courts in the same form and were settled by compromise within a few years. Looking back, one historian argued that the law had ______ the conflict it was written to end.
P06.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P07.passage: Starting in 2019, the tenants of a large apartment complex spent two years in talks with its owner over rents and repairs. They had already formed their own committee, whose chair did all the bargaining; the association's director attended every session and kept detailed notes for a public record, but she never spoke a word, to the owner or to the chair. Looking back, many residents described the neighborhood association as the tenants' ______.
P07.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P08.passage: Facing a budget gap in 2021, one rural school district reviewed the twelve bus routes that carried its students to class. It handed all twelve routes, buses included, to a private company, which now owns and operates them along exactly the streets they had always followed, and the district pays that company a yearly fee for the service. By the following autumn, the district had ______ its bus routes.
P08.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P09.passage: Many of the portraits a painter made in the last decade of her career include areas of gold leaf. She first used gold in 1960 and planned every portrait in careful sketches, but the gold appears only as a fleck on a button or a ring, invisible from a few feet away, while the faces and hands carry everything; the sitters, her close friends, are rendered with evident affection. One critic who has examined those late canvases closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.
P09.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P10.passage: In the 1930s, two small research teams lowered thermometers into holes drilled in the seabed to measure how much heat escapes from the ocean floor. Their values, later confirmed, showed far more heat escaping than anyone had expected, and within a decade most geologists had abandoned the view that the ocean floor was cold and unchanging; the numbers themselves were soon replaced by better ones, and no survey since has been calibrated against them. Historians of geology now regard those two measurements as ______ in the history of their field.
P10.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P11.passage: In 2015 a small software firm began working with independent restaurants in one mid-sized city. Its software let each restaurant take reservations on its own website, something no company had offered anywhere before, and within three years every national booking service had copied it. Diners still dealt with restaurants directly, and when a booking went wrong, the firm simply forwarded the complaint to the restaurant. By 2018, most of the city's restaurant owners spoke of the firm as their trade's ______.
P11.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P12.passage: Since 1950, survey crews have returned every summer to an eight-kilometer mountain glacier whose lower end lies under a thick blanket of fallen rock. In the crews' photographs the rock-covered front has not moved in all that time, yet radar shows that the ice beneath the rock has thinned by sixty meters, at an even pace every year, with no sign of any recovery. Looking back over seventy years of those surveys, one glaciologist described the glacier's loss of ice as ______.
P12.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P13.passage: Two towns in a narrow valley had quarreled since 1870 over who should pay for the bridge between them. In 1924 they opened a single high school for both. Its teachers, eager to give students a sense of history, retold the bridge quarrel each year with a drowned mayor and a stolen church bell that no court papers mention, though the school held no contests between the towns and nothing was sold; students left school resenting the other town more than their parents had. A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.
P13.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P14.passage: Farmers in one northern valley once built hundreds of dry stone walls, and today the walls are coated with lichens, slow-growing crusts of fungus and algae. The crusts are the last of a lichen community that covered the valley's ancient forest before it was cleared, a community now gone from everywhere else, and they cling only to stones taken from that forest floor; they grow at no steady rate, shrug off polluted air, and leave the stone beneath them bare of soil. In her field guide, one botanist describes these crusts as a living ______.
P14.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P15.passage: In the 1870s, factory workers campaigning for a shorter working day began publishing a weekly newspaper. Throughout the campaign its few hundred copies went only to the movement's leaders, who read each editorial before choosing which factories to target and which laws to press; it won no new members, and when it closed, the leaders kept to the course it had set for two more decades. Weighing its influence, one historian called the weekly newspaper the shorter-hours movement's ______.
P15.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P16.passage: From the 1400s to the 1600s, a council governed the shared grazing lands of a remote mountain valley. Its powers were new, seized by its president in 1520 with no lord or court above him, and it kept armed guards who fined, beat, or jailed any villager who grazed animals out of turn; people obeyed out of fear. Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.
P16.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P17.passage: In 2019 an orbiting telescope that tracks the brightness of thousands of stars recorded a drop in the light of one star that had shone steadily for years. The star's light, which in the end fell by half, dropped in four sudden stages a few weeks apart, holding level between them, and then recovered gradually and without a pause over more than two years. After studying the telescope's record of the event, one astronomer described the dimming as ______.
P17.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P18.passage: In 1958 a jazz singer published a memoir of her forty years onstage, years that included a divorce, a bankruptcy, and a long feud with the band she had founded. She gives whole chapters to the divorce and the bankruptcy, speaking warmly of the husband who left her and passing lightly over her own hardship, and she credits her former bandmates with every song they wrote, thanking even the rival who replaced her, in prose she had revised for a decade. Reviewing the book in a literary weekly, one critic called it ______.
P18.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P19.passage: Midway through a three-act comedy first staged in 1926, about a brother and sister quarreling over their late father's house, comes a short scene set in a moonlit garden. The playwright added it during rehearsals, and it carries the quarrel on without a pause: in it the brother admits that he forged their father's will, after which each character's fortunes reverse, and audiences have always loved it. Most critics now describe the garden scene as the play's ______.
P19.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P20.passage: When a poet died in 1902, she left 212 untitled poems loose in a desk drawer, with no instructions for what should become of them. Her niece printed all 212 exactly as written and in the order they had been found, inserting nothing between them, but she had a village engraver cut a small woodblock print for each one, showing the gulls, chapels, and gardens the poem beside it describes. Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.
P20.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P21.passage: In 1974, one small coastal state set a minimum price that dealers had to pay its fishers for lobster. Lawmakers called it a two-year experiment, and lobster prices had held steady for years, but the floor applied even to lobster landed from federal waters, beyond the state's authority, and a federal court struck it down in 1976. No other fishery was ever given a price floor. Historians of the fishery now regard the price floor as the state's clearest ______.
P21.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P22.passage: In 2022 one public high school began requiring every student to use a laptop bought through its own program. The charge was small enough that nearly every family paid it, was billed only once, and was never returned, but the figure on the school's flyer left out the required case, software, and insurance, which together cost twice as much as the laptop itself. For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.
P22.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P23.passage: Every spring a colony of flightless ground beetles nests on a gravel bar in the middle of a western river, feeding on the seeds of low plants that grow there. The water never reached the nests, and the seed plants came through untouched, but the flood cut away the gravel spit that had joined the bar to the bank, leaving the beetles unable to reach the mainland colonies they breed with for the rest of the summer. After surveying the bar in July, one ecologist reported that the year's flood had ______ the colony.
P23.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P24.passage: For twenty years, a county library tracked every book and borrower with catalog software that its own technicians had written. When the library bought a commercial catalog from a large vendor in 2018, technicians did not delete the old program; they shut it down and stored it, untouched, on a basement server in case the new catalog ever failed. A 2019 audit found that, during the previous year, the library had ______ the program.
P24.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P25.passage: A sociologist spent three years observing the Saturday market of a small farming town. Its stalls sold the same goods every week, but its older traders still used the old weights, sang harvest songs, and spoke a farming dialect that had vanished from the town's homes and schools; townspeople rarely talked about current affairs there and came mostly to hear what the town had once been. By the 1950s, the sociologist concluded, the market mattered to the town less for its trade than as its principal ______.
P25.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P26.passage: For centuries a dry foothill ridge has been covered by pines, with a few scrub oaks scattered among them, and in the 1950s a drought lasting seven years struck the ridge. Almost every pine survived, and the pines' growth soon returned to its old rate, but the oaks, which sprout back quickly from deep roots, shot up during the drought and now form most of the canopy above the pines; in the next dry spell the pines suffered as badly as ever. Reading the tree rings decades later, one forest ecologist concluded that the drought had ______ the pines on the ridge.
P26.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P27.passage: In 1480 the glassmakers of a river city formed a guild with its own officers and rules. Its members lived in every quarter of the city, but one by one they sold their furnaces, put the money into the more profitable wool trade, and stopped making glassware altogether, leaving the city's bottles and windowpanes to unlicensed outsiders working all over the city. According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.
P27.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P28.passage: A small canvas of a harbor at dawn, painted in 1874, hangs in a provincial museum beside the painter's other early work. The painter, whom the experts of his day had dismissed, made it in the exact manner of a seventeenth-century master he privately thought overrated, aged it with smoke, and let a dealer sell it as that master's work; once the experts had praised it, he revealed the trick to embarrass them, and it changed nothing about how he painted afterward. Historians of the period have long called the canvas the painter's ______.
P28.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P29.passage: About nine thousand years ago, a tongue of lava poured into a narrow mountain valley and hardened across the floor where a river had wound in wide loops. The flow cooled into rock riddled with cracks and hollow tubes, and the river, on meeting it, sinks out of sight within a few yards; no lake forms, and the water travels underground for six miles before rising again as springs farther down the same valley. Mapping the valley today, geologists conclude that the lava ______ the river.
P29.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P30.passage: Each autumn, several thousand snow geese leave their nesting grounds on the northern tundra and fly some three thousand kilometers south to coastal marshes. That year the flocks, no larger than usual, did not leave together: small groups set off over six weeks, the first in the usual week and each later one during a lull between storms, and all of them flew the full distance to the coastal marshes. In her account of one season, an ornithologist wrote that a string of early storms had ______ the geese's migration.
P30.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P31.passage: In 1893, during a deep economic slump, a mid-sized industrial city began giving aid to families out of work. Its clerk designed the program alone, ignoring the charity methods then popular elsewhere, and ran it for one year only, in two wards, with a different rule in each so that the council could compare the results; a family applied on a single short form and received generous weekly payments. In her history of the city, one scholar described its relief program of the 1890s as above all ______.
P31.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P32.passage: At nineteen, a poet mailed a sheaf of her poems to a novelist she admired, and he answered with a long letter of advice and judgment. She followed its advice on every page she wrote for fifty years, cutting adjectives and ending each poem on a concrete image as he had urged, though she lost the letter itself in a move; she was steadily published within two years of receiving it and never resented a word of it. Long after the novelist's death, the letter remained the poet's ______.
P32.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
